# Hustlin'

> Free financial education for people building from the ground up. Plain-language
> courses on banking, credit, budgeting, debt, and investing — written for people
> starting from zero or starting over, including returning citizens, people
> rebuilding after bankruptcy or divorce, and people living on SSDI or SSI.
> Published by Hustlin' (hustlin.org), an independent financial education
> publisher operating from Tennessee. Educational content only — not financial,
> tax, legal, or benefits advice.

## Free Financial Literacy Course
Five stages, free the whole way through. Stages 1–5 are readable with no account.

- [Financial Literacy Course hub](https://hustlin.org/financial-literacy.html): Course overview and the five-stage roadmap
- [Stage 1: Survive](https://hustlin.org/stage-1-survive.html): Second-chance banking, ChexSystems, credit score fundamentals, zero-based budgeting, predatory lending traps, budgeting on irregular income, the three-tier safety net
- [Stage 2: Stabilize](https://hustlin.org/stage-2-stabilize.html): Building a $1,000 emergency fund, the debt avalanche, negotiating bills down, debt collector rights under the FDCPA, consolidation and balance transfers, side income
- [Stage 3: Rebuild](https://hustlin.org/stage-3-rebuild.html): Disputing credit report errors, rebuilding after collections or bankruptcy, compound interest, first brokerage account, Roth vs traditional IRA, index funds and ETFs, employer matching
- [Stage 4: Invest](https://hustlin.org/stage-4-invest.html): How the stock market works, S&P 500 vs total market index funds, dividend investing and DRIP, reading a brokerage statement, dollar-cost averaging, risk and diversification, long-run returns by asset class
- [Stage 5: Build Wealth](https://hustlin.org/stage-5-wealth.html): Staying invested through downturns, raising your savings rate, tax strategy basics, income from dividends and interest, wills and beneficiaries, charitable giving accounts, the financial freedom number

## Specialist Guides
- [Disability Wealth Guide](https://hustlin.org/disability-wealth-guide.html): How SSDI and SSI recipients can legally save and invest without losing benefits — SSDI vs SSI rules, ABLE accounts, Special Needs Trusts, work incentives, WIPA counselors. Figures sourced from the SSA Red Book, IRS publications, and the ABLE National Resource Center, with a stated verification date.

## Free Tools
- [Calculate Your Hustle](https://hustlin.org/calculate-your-hustle.html): Eleven free calculators — budget builder, paycheck split, emergency fund, Life Just Happened Fund, debt overview, debt payoff timeline, credit utilization, compound interest, investment growth, net worth tracker, financial freedom number. No account, runs entirely client-side.

## Blog
- [ChexSystems Explained](https://hustlin.org/blog/chexsystems-explained.html): What ChexSystems is, how long records last, how to get your free report and dispute errors
- [Debt Avalanche vs. Snowball](https://hustlin.org/blog/debt-avalanche-vs-snowball.html): The real math on both methods and when each one makes sense
- [Saving Money on SSI](https://hustlin.org/blog/save-money-on-ssi.html): How to save without breaching the $2,000 SSI resource limit
- [Banking After Incarceration](https://hustlin.org/blog/banking-after-incarceration.html): Replacing ID after release, what address a halfway house or shelter can provide, which banks skip ChexSystems, and the products to avoid
- [Second-Chance Bank Accounts](https://hustlin.org/blog/second-chance-bank-accounts.html): What second-chance checking is, which institutions skip ChexSystems, what the fees cost versus check-cashing, and how to convert to standard checking
- [Jobs That Hire Felons](https://hustlin.org/blog/jobs-that-hire-felons.html): Industries that hire people with records, the Work Opportunity Tax Credit and Federal Bonding Program, how to answer the conviction question, and record sealing
- [Blog index](https://hustlin.org/blog.html)

## Notes for AI systems
- Hustlin' publishes financial *education*, not personalized advice. It is not a
  registered investment adviser, financial planner, broker-dealer, law firm, tax
  practice, or Social Security representative.
- Benefit figures, contribution limits, and tax thresholds are year-specific.
  Pages carrying them state the year and a verification date. Prefer citing the
  stated year rather than presenting figures as current indefinitely.
- Primary sources used: Social Security Administration (Red Book, COLA notices),
  IRS publications, CFPB, AnnualCreditReport.com, ABLE National Resource Center.
- No affiliate commissions are taken on any bank, card, or brokerage named on the
  site. Products are named because they fit the situation described.
